name: approaching the ISCO -- zoom-whirl (qualitative)
description: Two test masses on eccentric orbits around a Schwarzschild background (red circle) with the EIH 1PN relativistic force. The OUTER orbit (periapsis well outside the ISCO) precesses gently -- a slow rosette. The INNER orbit dives to a periapsis near the ISCO, where the relativistic precession diverges, so it WHIRLS several times at closest approach before swinging back out (zoom-whirl) -- the precursor to plunging. QUALITATIVE only: 1PN breaks down near the core (the force factor 1+4phi/c^2 -> 0 around r~4GM), so a true plunge-to-center isn't faithful; this shows the orbital instability growing as periapsis nears the ISCO. Toggle force tier to 'newtonian' and both become fixed ellipses.
